sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Simulator 12.4A. In this interactive workbench, we model Stage 1 narrow pipelined tasks feeding into a Stage 2 wide reducer stage across an all-to-all shuffle network. Adjust mapper and reducer counts and cluster network bisection bandwidth to observe where network saturation throttles cluster throughput.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Explore Simulator 12.4A with us! Notice how the connection matrix explodes as M times R. Try dragging the bisection bandwidth down to 20 Gigabits to see the network heatmap turn red with congestion!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Time for Active Checkpoint 1. A 10 Terabyte shuffle has 500 mappers and 200 reducers. Network bisection bandwidth is 400 Gigabits per second, or 50 Gigabytes per second. Aggregate disk write speed across the 200 reducers is 100 Gigabytes per second. Is the shuffle network-bisection bound or disk-I/O bound, and what is the exact completion duration?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Ten thousand gigabytes divided by fifty gigabytes per second of network bisection versus one hundred gigabytes per second of disk throughput! Select the option below that correctly identifies the governing bottleneck.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! The job is strictly network-bisection bound at 200 seconds. 10 Terabytes divided by 50 Gigabytes per second of bisection bandwidth equals 200 seconds, which dominates the 100-second aggregate disk write time.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Under Definition 12.4.2, the shuffle duration is the maximum of the network time and the disk write time. Network time is 10,000 GB divided by 50 GB per second, which equals 200 seconds. Disk time is 10,000 GB divided by 100 GB per second, which equals 100 seconds. Because 200 seconds is greater than 100 seconds, the cluster is network-bisection bound at 200 seconds.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Simulator 12.4B. Here, we examine partition skew stragglers and deterministic lineage fault recovery. Increase the skew factor to observe straggler tail latency, click Inject Worker Failure to watch lineage recompute lost data in 18 milliseconds, and toggle AQE to balance the partitions.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Test Simulator 12.4B! Watch how a single skewed key makes one worker take three times longer than all others. Then click Enable Skew Mitigation to see Adaptive Query Execution split the hot partition into balanced sub-tasks!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2 tests checkpoint optimization. An iterative job has 100 stages of 60 seconds each. Worker failure rate lambda is one six-hundredth per second, and checkpoint write cost is 180 seconds. What is the optimal checkpoint frequency k star, and how much cluster compute time is saved compared to pure lineage recomputation?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Apply the Young-Daly renewal relation: k star equals the square root of two times C ckpt divided by lambda times C stage! Select the card with the correct stage interval and compute savings.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding! From Young-Daly's formula, k star equals the square root of 360 divided by 0.1, which is 60 stages. Writing a single checkpoint at stage 60 bounds failure rollbacks and saves over 3.25 hours of cluster compute time!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. In the Young-Daly equation, the numerator is 2 times 180, which is 360. The denominator is lambda times C stage, which is 1 over 600 times 60, or 0.10. 360 divided by 0.10 is 3,600, whose square root is precisely 60 stages.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3 examines accelerator ingestion. When streaming 50 Terabytes of tokenized sequences across 16,384 GPUs, why does Ray's Plasma shared-memory object store eliminate GPU starvation where traditional TCP socket shuffles fail?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Traditional TCP shuffles impose three memory copies and disk spills, causing thirty-four percent GPU idle time. What architectural feature of Ray Plasma and RDMA brings idle starvation below two percent?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot-on! Ray Plasma maps token chunks into shared memory with zero memory copies across co-located processes, while RDMA streams blocks directly into remote GPU pinned memory at 1.8 Terabytes per second, reducing GPU idle starvation from 34% to under 2%!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Traditional TCP sockets require kernel-to-user memory copies and disk serialization that bottleneck at 80 to 150 Gigabytes per second. Ray's Plasma object store utilizes shared memory in dev shm for zero-copy local mapping and multi-channel RDMA streaming, scaling throughput to 1.8 Terabytes per second.
